uses: Ticket/RFC identity, hierarchy, relationships and lifecycle command availability
Objective/Task plan, grouping, execution, review and correction projections
CPL/SLA classification, calculation and report evidence
Inventory lifecycle actions, warnings, bulk partitions and physical consequence projections
accepted revisions and optional recoverable working-copy persistence

provides: UI security envelope, secret redaction/display boundaries and local-session interaction surfaces

forbidden_dependencies: Unsaved UI state cannot affect authoritative counts, SLA, matching, inventory availability, relationships or reports.
A hold animation/dialog/selection cannot authorize a domain command without current server/domain validation.
Responsive reflow cannot remove or change business capability or evidence meaning.
UI may not duplicate canonical Communication bodies into ticket/request records.
UI may not silently merge identities while consolidating relationship context.
Theme/skin choices cannot alter workflow, command names/availability, status meaning or accessibility.
command_boundary: The client submits explicit command intent plus target identity, accepted base revision and required inputs. The host/domain revalidates authorization, revision, dependencies and business invariants. On success the client replaces/reconciles its projection from authoritative result; on failure the working copy remains non-authoritative and safe for review/retry.
